script.text: OpenAI's top models just landed on a rival's cloud. What changes for companies?

On October twenty-first, Google Cloud said it is adding three OpenAI models to its Model Garden: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Axios reports it starts as a private preview for select enterprise customers.

Here is what changes. Companies can buy the models through Google Cloud Marketplace, and Axios reports the spending can count toward existing cloud commitments. Google says prompts and outputs stay inside customer data perimeters and are not used to train foundation models.

Reports describe Google Cloud as the third big U.S. cloud to sell OpenAI models, after Microsoft and Amazon. OpenAI says general availability is planned in the coming weeks. Per-token prices have not been published.
Will most companies now buy A.I. models from several clouds? Yes or no?
